messages:
arun: FYI I found a reproducible correctness divergence when activation quantization is enabled + mixed-precision GEMM routing on recent runtime build. output logits drift after first KV warmup on long prompts.

marta: ugh, does this look like the fp8 codepath or a scheduling/regression in the kernel selector?

arun: seems tied to the activation quant path (we enable act-quant + bf16 fallback). repro cmd below, tiny script that runs streaming with kv caching enabled and compares logits after layer 12.

arun: ```bash
# repro (A100, cuda 11.8)
python -m runtime.client --model redwood-open-7b --quant act8 --mixed bf16,fp8 --seq 2048 --stream --prompt-file tests/long_prompt.txt 
> artifacts/logits_before.npy
# run twice to warm KV and compare
```

lee: can you paste the minimal diff between expected vs observed? numbers/seed?

arun: seed=42, single-batch size=1. After warmup, token 512 onward logit mean deviates by ~1.2e-2 (not catastrophic) but causes downstream sampling change in 5% cases. checksum of matmul outputs on layer 11 shows bitflips in low-magnitude lanes.

ryan: any nvprof/nsys evidence? kernel mismatch or race?

arun: attached simple nvtx traces: kernel chosen switches from int8_gemm_cu to mixed_gemm_fp8 for some layers depending on per-layer scale calibration. I think the calibration thresholds are causing inconsistent kernel selection when kv cache is reused across requests.

sophia: ops-bot flagged related nightly perf job: ops-bot: nightly/perf/mixed-precision-flaky failed (regression +3% error rate). ci-bot: added assertion to catch non-deterministic checksum drift.

marta: that sounds like nondeterministic kernel routing in the same process when cache is present. Maybe cal_table is being updated at runtime and influences selector. Are we mutating global quant state during request handling?

arun: yes — quant calibration table gets lazily updated on first forward for a shard. If another request hits the same shard with warm KV, kernel_selector sees different calibration and picks fp8 variant mid-stream.

lee: repro idea: force calibration to be precomputed at model load time in CI and see if regression disappears. If it does, that's our race.

arun: I ran that locally: precompute_calibration=true => no drift, consistent kernel choice, checksums match baseline.

ryan: good find. still want to know why fp8 gemm has low-magnitude differences only when interleaved with cached KV. Could be packing alignment or offset applied to activation scales. Any evidence in the packed kernel header?

arun: yes, packing header for KV uses a different scale quant index path when the KV buffer is reused; small off-by-one in index used for scale lookup in kernel_args. That explains lane-level tiny differences.

marta: propose short term: 1) revert lazy-calibration change so calibration happens on model init, 2) add atomic update to cal_table and freeze it during inference, 3) add CI test with kv-warm sequences + mixed precision.

ryan: agree. also add asserts in kernel_selector to log when kernel choice changes mid-request for same layer idx across steps. That will catch similar future regressions.

sophia: I'll file an incident ticket for the perf/regression triage and tag infra for canary rollout hold.

arun: patch PR coming: revert lazy calibrator + unit test (will include repro script and nvtx trace dump).

marta: add a short perf note in the PR explaining expected perf uplift tradeoffs so product knows we disabled lazy calibration (possible higher startup cost).

ops-bot: canary/policy: paused deployment for branch runtime/main until regression PR merges. :rotating_light:

ryan: once PR is up I'll run 24h mixed-precision nightly and KV-heavy load to be safe. Thanks for the quick triage.

arun: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321 — includes test reproducer and nsys captures.

marta: LGTM after small comment. let's get that merged and revert the canary hold after one successful canary. :thumbsup:
